---
title: "DT[, v] does not select the columns whose names v holds"
ref: DT-01
categories: [data.table]
impact: cryptique
attendu: "columns a and b"
versions: "All versions of {data.table}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2019)"
---

::: {.piege packages="data.table"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))

dt <- data.table(a = 1:2, b = 3:4, v = c("x", "y"))
v <- c("a", "b")
dt[, v]

columns <- function() {
  c("a", "b")
}
dt[, columns()]
dt[, c(columns())]
```
:::

## Why

In `dt[, j]`, `j` is an expression evaluated **inside** the table, as in `with()`. There, `v` refers first to the column `v`, and `dt[, v]` returns its content. `columns()` returns a character vector, which {data.table} hands back as is: it is a computed result, not a selection.

{data.table} adds convenience rules that make the whole thing unpredictable: a `j` reduced to a symbol with no column of that name gives an error suggesting `..v`, and a `c()` around a function call is enough to trigger a column selection.

## The fix

Say explicitly that `j` holds column names, with the `..` prefix or `with = FALSE`.

::: {.piege packages="data.table"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(data.table))

dt[, ..v]
dt[, columns(), with = FALSE]
```
:::
